newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA LEU STABLE, C.BANK TAKES LEU FUNDS.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA LEU STABLE, C.BANK TAKES LEU FUNDS.

text.p: The Romanian leu closed Monday stable at about 7,180/220 to the dollar with the central bank (BNR) purchasing excesses of dollars and draining leu liquidity to keep interest rates attractive, traders said.
The BNR confirmed it had taken up 525 billion lei worth of money market funds from six commercial banks at rates ranging from 48 to 68 percent.
Traders hailed the BNR move, saying this would soak up excesses of leu liquidity which have put interest rates under pressure to move down fairly quickly in the past week.
"This will balance the market and keep monetary policy goals under control," said one trader.

The money market has been overliquid in recent weeks following BNR purchases of excess dollars triggered by rising interest in Romanian equities and securities. Short-term rates slipped towards 45 percent from some 190 percent in April.
Last week, the government allowed the BNR to take leu deposits from commercial banks in a move to implement open-market operations to conduct monetary policy.
